description.value: The study examined behavioral and neural markers of cigarette-craving regulation in young-adult daily smokers before and after smoking, using a proximal/distal perspective-taking fMRI task with smoking and non-smoking videos.

value: We expected fronto-striatal activation related to craving regulation to diminish from before to after smoking, assuming that reduced craving after smoking a cigarette will result in less engagement of neural mechanisms to regulate craving.
We expected an interaction of close/far instruction and video type (smoke/non-smoke), with the greatest craving occurring during the close, smoke condition.

description.value: Participants were scanned after overnight abstinence before and after smoking their first cigarette of the day; the study included repeated testing sessions and a within-subject comparison of smoking state.

spans.text: Participants were scanned before and after smoking their first cigarette of the day, a cigarette of their preferred brand, ~35 min before performing the task in the scanner.

value: Comparison of cue-induced activation (smoking vs. non-smoking videos) before vs. after smoking revealed activation in rostral and caudal anterior cingulate cortex, including the subgenual segment, left inferior frontal gyrus, and bilateral superior and middle temporal gyri.

The interaction was primarily driven by a smoking-related reduction in activation for smoking cues and not non-smoking cues. No regions showed significantly increased activation due to smoking a cigarette.
